key_insight: The paper introduces Quantum Fidelity-per-Cost (QFC), a metric that blends output fidelity, shot count, and monetary cost so quantum backends can be compared by practical value rather than fidelity alone.
engineering_relevance: For cloud quantum users and procurement teams, QFC highlights that the cheapest or most accurate device may not be the best overall choice once provider billing is included.
method: Measured circuit execution fidelity across 14 cloud QPU access-path entries spanning 12 physical QPUs.
Compared four access ecosystems: AWS, IBM Quantum Runtime, IQM Resonance, and Oxford Quantum Circuits.
Defined QFC using KL divergence from an ideal distribution plus shot count and cost under documented billing models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a cross-provider study and shows that backend rankings can change when price is included, with results evaluated across 14 access-path entries.
watch_item: QFC depends on provider-specific pricing and billing rules, so scores can shift as prices change or new machines are added.
paper_title: Quantum Fidelity-per-Cost: A Metric for Evaluation of Quantum Computing Systems
